_comment: What you want, as opposed to sources.json which is where to look. bootstrap-sources.js rewrites sources.json wholesale but never touches this file, so edits here survive a re-bootstrap.
_maxAgeDays: How far back to look, in days. You do not edit this by hand: it is written here the moment you change the dashboard's 'Posted within' control, and everything that cares about dates reads it from here - the ingest gate, the on-screen feed, and scripts/rescore.js. null means no age limit (the control's 'Any age').
_archiveAfterDays: How long a posting you never acted on stays in the feed before a run sweeps it to 'archived'. Different question from maxAgeDays: that one is how old a posting was when it was found, this one is how long we keep showing it. Archiving is reversible from the dashboard's Restore button.
_roleKeywords: A posting must match one of these in its title to be ingested at all. Tier 1 pulls a company's ENTIRE board, so without this gate you get welders and accountants alongside the engineering roles.
_levelKeywords: New-grad signals. Not required, but they raise the score, and a title carrying one satisfies the role gate on its own.
_gradKeywords: Graduate-program titles that clear the role gate on their own, since such a posting may name no engineering discipline at all. Deliberately narrower than levelKeywords: letting "associate" or "entry level" through the gate pulled in support and production-technician roles from the real corpus.
_timingKeywords: Your Jan 2027 start window. Scored, never required — most postings never state a start date, and requiring it would empty the feed.
_excludeTitleKeywords: Seniority markers. Matched on word boundaries, so 'Lead' is excluded but 'Leadership' is not.
_locationWeights: Your stated preference mix. Used two ways: normalized against the largest weight they become the location half of match_score, and as-is they set the proportions of the default balanced feed. A location deleted from this object is genuinely gone - the defaults are NOT merged back over it.
_locationWeightsOrder: Order matters on a tie. Calgary and remote are both 0.35, and a posting matching several buckets takes the first of the highest-weighted ones - so 'Calgary, AB / Remote' is filed as Calgary, which is right: it is a job you could do from an office you can drive to.
_remoteMeaning: The remote bucket is not just the word 'remote' in a location field. A posting only counts as remote if it is (a) not US-fenced, since US-remote would need a TN visa, and (b) not actually hybrid, which only the description reveals. See lib/remote.js. A hybrid role in Calgary still buckets as Calgary - hybrid is fine when the office is the one you can drive to.
_offListLocations: drop = a posting whose location resolves to none of the buckets above is never ingested. Postings with no location string at all are kept, bucketed as 'unknown', and sorted after the balanced feed.
_workAuth: You do not hold US work authorization. A US-restricted posting (Seattle, or a remote role fenced to the US) that never mentions sponsorship gets its location score multiplied by this, so it stops consuming your 5% Seattle share.
_scoreWeights: match_score = locationWeight * location + keywordWeight * keywords. Location leads because it is the constraint you were most specific about.
